Class Serve

java.lang.Object
com.lloseng.ocsf.server.AbstractServer
com.andreibel.server.controller.Serve
All Implemented Interfaces:
Runnable
public class Serve extends com.lloseng.ocsf.server.AbstractServer
Main OCSF server implementation for the Bistro system.

This class extends AbstractServer and provides the networking entry point for the server: it receives objects from clients, expects them to be Message instances, routes them by Message.getType() to the appropriate controller, and sends a response back to the client.

Routing

Requests are dispatched using a switch on the message type, delegating to:

  • OrderController - orders and availability-related requests
  • SubscriberController - subscriber login, CRUD and order history
  • WorkerController - worker login, restaurant configuration and layout
  • WaitingController - waiting list flows and reports

GUI integration

If a BistroServerGUIController is attached via setGUIController(BistroServerGUIController), connection lifecycle events are forwarded to the GUI so it can display current client states.

Threading note

OCSF callbacks may run on non-JavaFX threads. If the GUI controller updates JavaFX UI controls, it should wrap the updates using javafx.application.Platform.runLater(...).

Andrei Beloziyorove

    • handleMessageFromClient

      protected void handleMessageFromClient(Object msg, com.lloseng.ocsf.server.ConnectionToClient client)
      Handles an incoming object received from a specific client connection.

      The OCSF framework calls this method whenever a client sends an object. This implementation:

      1. Validates the object is a Message.
      2. Logs the request via TUI.serverInputLog(Message).
      3. Routes by message.getType() to the corresponding controller handler.
      4. Logs the response via TUI.serverOutputLog(Message).
      5. Sends the response back to the client with ConnectionToClient.sendToClient(Object).

      Important: some handlers may return null (for example, if the request is treated as a server-side-only action). In that case, sending null may not be desirable. Consider guarding with if (response != null) sendToClient(response).

      Specified by:
      handleMessageFromClient in class com.lloseng.ocsf.server.AbstractServer
      Parameters:
      msg - object received from the client (expected to be a Message)
      client - client connection that sent the object
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if the incoming object is not a Message or an IOException occurs while sending the response
